intended_object: The empirical Rademacher correlation of a binary hypothesis h with a sign vector σ ∈ {±1}^m on a sample x₁,…,x_m, i.e. (1/m) Σᵢ σᵢ h(xᵢ), where the Boolean labels and signs are read as ±1. This is the quantity whose supremum over the class, averaged over σ, gives the empirical Rademacher complexity. Inferred from the docstring, the name and its use in `EmpiricalRademacherComplexity`.
explanation:
The body computes (1/m) Σ_{i : Fin m} s(σᵢ)·s(h(xᵢ)), where `boolToSign` sends true to 1 and false to -1. So Boolean signs act as Rademacher ±1 variables and Boolean labels as ±1 hypothesis outputs, which is the textbook normalized correlation used in Rademacher complexity for binary classification. When m = 0 the definition returns 0. This matches what (1/0)·(empty sum) would give in Mathlib anyway, so the special case has no effect. The library's lemma |corr| ≤ 1 and its use in `EmpiricalRademacherComplexity` (sup over h ∈ C, averaged uniformly over the 2^m sign vectors) agree with the standard definition.

Rademacher complexity can also be defined for real-valued function classes. However, this library works with Boolean concept classes (`Concept X Bool`), and the ±1 encoding of labels is part of the binary-classification version of the notion, so this is not an unjustified narrowing. Mathlib has no Rademacher complexity or Rademacher correlation: its "Rademacher" files are about Rademacher's theorem on differentiability of Lipschitz functions. So there is no more general Mathlib construction this definition should have used.
